name: review-lens replay set
howToRun: scripts/review-replay.mjs prints what each reviewer gets and scores what comes back; .claude/workflows/review-replay.js fans it out. For each PR a lens runs on, the reviewer gets only `git diff base head` plus read access to the tree at `head`, with no GitHub reads, no docs/LESSONS.md or docs/IDEAS.md, no later commits and no file:line hints, and the lens text with its real examples removed. Scored per PR (a PR with two defects counts once), per facet: a hit is a high or medium finding on `defect.file`, an upper bound until someone reads that it names the same mechanism; a finding on a control counts against the lens, except on a control marked trapFor that facet, which is read by hand. The 21 correctness PRs were produced by the audit's own reviewer + two-refuter design on Fable, so re-running that design re-finds them: a new lens's number must come from the reuse, performance, security and context cases, which no standing reviewer found.
howThisCouldFlatterALens: Incumbent advantage: every correctness case was found by post-merge-audit.js on 2026-10-27 at the deep (Fable) tier; replaying the same prompt on the same PRs measures recall of a known answer, not yield on new merges. Compare against the clean controls from the same surge, never alone.
Leakage: each defect has a public issue naming file:line and a later fix PR on main. A lens with GitHub access, or a tree newer than `head`, can read the answer. Run offline at `head`.

Path prior: 11 of 22 correctness defects sit under src/trading, src/server, src/storage or scripts/moneypenny. A lens that flags those paths blindly looks good; the controls deliberately come from the same paths (#6303 storage, #6300 boot, #6294 server, #6225 and #6227 moneypenny).
Date skew: performance cases are Aug to Oct 5 PRs, controls are Oct 26 to 27. File age or size must not be an input.

Reuse cases are mechanical: `git grep` at `base` for the pasted name finds them with no model. The honest question for a model lens is whether it adds judgment (same concept, or a homonym; pct in #4443 takes a fraction, render-atoms' pct takes a percent) over the script, not whether it finds the name.

Performance ground truth is the later `npm run stability:budget` number, which the replay cannot run per case cheaply (an 180-day x 12-account seed in a 512 MB container). A lens is scored on naming the mechanism (a request path re-reading a whole growing ledger), not on predicting milliseconds.

Security cases are unexploited: S1 and S2 are the study's readings of the code, not incidents. Confidence is stated per case; a lens that misses them is not proven wrong, and one that finds them is not proven right until the fixture in tests/scripts/moneypenny/work-mode.spec.ts exists.

Controls are 'no confirmed finding'; batches B, C and D of the audit lost their low findings before writing them out (#6330), so a low-severity true positive on a control is possible. Count only high/medium findings against controls.
Fix-PR controls (#6294, #6296, #6299, #6300, #6302, #6303) close audit issues; a lens reading the linked issue learns the defect area. The eval strips PR bodies.

The lenses were written from this set: most smells' real examples are cases here. The prompt strips each lens's Real: clauses, but the smell itself is still shaped by the answer, so recall on these cases is an upper bound on recall on new PRs. Only a run on PRs the lens was not grown from can say otherwise.

The structure facet has five borrowed correctness cases (D08, D13, D14, D19, D20), labelled by one reader, and its clean labels on controls are an assumption: a small fix PR with no structural finding on record, which nobody read for structure. Treat a structure finding on a control as a candidate to read, and structure recall as thin.

This replay runs reviewers only, not the two refuters. Findings on controls are counted before any refuter, so they overstate manufacture compared with the audit; the one-in-three survival number in each lens's kill rule cannot come from here.
A hit is matched by file. A reviewer that flags the right file for the wrong reason counts until someone reads it and sets mechanism: false on that finding.

docs/review/REVIEW.md, which the pre-merge lens reads, was written by a session that had read this set. A spec bars it from naming a case's PR or file, and its per-path notes state each path's contract, not a case's mechanism, but a note can still point at a case's class. Only a replay with the notes removed (the workflow's args.rulesFile) can say what they add.

A file match can count a finding the pre-merge job could never post: 5 of the 21 correctness defects (D01, D03, D14, D19, D20) sit in a file their PR never changed. The pre-merge score counts hits in the diff apart and passes only on those; a defect named at its caller counts only on reading.

The ia facet was labelled by the session that wrote its lens, from the #895 cluster and the /outpost reshuffle, and each smell's shape came from these cases (#6886 slice 2). Its controls are route and nav PRs whose placement held or executed a written decision; two of them (K18, K21) were later re-homed by a newer decision, so a key or second-home finding there is a trap read by hand, not manufacture. Seven of its nine PRs predate docs/IA.md (2026-09-26), so the lens is judged there on its smells alone. A tenth, #815, was dropped after the first run: it was labelled from #819's body ('/outpost unreachable since #815'), but at #815's head the topbar still links /outpost, so the reviewer that cleared it was right and the label was wrong. A label taken from a later PR's prose is checked against the tree before it counts. I05 was labelled K19, a control, until the first run flagged a dead /app/outpost link in it and #3573 was found fixing exactly that; it is a defect the lens found, so it never counts toward the recall measured on the labels set before the run. On I04 the label names __root.tsx (the tab), and the run named the story order in edition-story.tsx at medium and the tab at low: a file match scores it low-only, a reading scores it a hit.

facets.correctness: wrong result, crash, broken contract, a requirement the code does not meet (post-merge-audit.js's lens today)
facets.reuse: a top-level symbol or block this PR defines that already exists elsewhere in the tree at base
facets.performance: a request or boot path that re-reads a whole growing ledger, or asks a store once per row
facets.security: a trust boundary crossed without the check the rest of the repo applies (author, scope, secret origin)
facets.context-loop: a change to CLAUDE.md, a skill, an agent, a hook, a workflow or the loop registry read for startup cost, a claim the named code does not hold, a rule with no reader, a loop with no number, a verifier whose unknown reads as a verdict
facets.structure: a concept with no named home, a second rule beside the one predicate, a hand-synced copy: the smells-and-patterns lens
facets.ia: a route left with no link from any page, data placed at a key it is not fetched by, a home or name that contradicts docs/IA.md at the head, a second home for what a page already holds: the information-architecture lens (#6886 slice 2)
